clearedSpotChecks.note: Fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/go-ethereum/master/core/state_transition.go on 2026-11-27: execute() starts at line 634, calls StartTxHook at 635, returns at 638-646 when endTxNow is set, and calls st.state.Prepare only at line 736. Fetched core/state/statedb.go: Prepare is at line 1571 and sets s.transientStorage = newTransientStorage() at line 1599. Fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/nitro/master/arbos/tx_processor.go: StartTxHook (line 197) returns true for the deposit branch (237-268, where the comment at 262-264 says the EVM is not invoked and only core.Transfer moves value), the internal branch (269-275) and the submit retryable branch (276-537); grep finds no evm.Call in 290-570, and auto redeems are returned through ScheduledTxes and applied as their own messages. The ArbitrumRetryTx branch (538-569) returns false on success, so the redeem runs through Prepare. Transient storage therefore starts empty for every transaction that can reach src/libraries/Lock.sol, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol, CurrencyDelta.sol and CurrencyReserves.sol. The endpoints serve the unpublished rc.9 b72783f build (web3_clientVersion queried by me on arb1.arbitrum.io and rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com), so master is a proxy for that build; the mined swap and replay checks are the evidence for the build actually running.

clearedSpotChecks.check: What the PoolManager's take and sync shapes do against the P256VERIFY precompile at 0x100, ArbSys (0x64) and ArbRetryableTx (0x6e), called from the PoolManager address by eth_call.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I widened the sweep on arb1.arbitrum.io with eth_call from the PoolManager address 0x360e...fb32 to 0x01-0x11, 0x64-0x74 and 0xff for transfer(PM,1) and balanceOf(PM). 0x01 and 0x6a (eth_getCode 0x, no precompile) return empty success; 0x02 and 0x03 return one hash word; 0x04 echoes the calldata; 0x05-0x11 fail on input; 0x64-0x74 revert or refuse; 0xff says debug precompiles are disabled. None of these lets take pay out value it did not debit: src/PoolManager.sol:291-297 debits the caller before currency.transfer, and src/types/Currency.sol:64-74 accepts only a first return word equal to 1 with at least 32 bytes, or empty return data. For 0x02, 0x03 and 0x04 the first word is not 1, so take reverts. For 0x04, balanceOf decodes a constant word (selector plus the PoolManager address), so sync then settle gives paid = 0 in src/PoolManager.sol:349-365. For empty-return addresses, balanceOfSelf at Currency.sol:94 cannot decode and sync reverts. Ethereum has the same answers at 0x01-0x11 and at 0x100 after Osaka, so none of this is a network difference, and a pool naming such a currency holds no other users' value.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Cycle 32 rerun of battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py (250), pmdiff2.py (300), swaps.py, replay.py and callsem.py on the three official endpoints, with web3_clientVersion recorded before each stage.
clearedSpotChecks.note: The logs in cycles/032/arbitrum-family.work/raw show 99,985 and 85,544 vectors with 0 mismatches and 0 errors on all three chains, 300 of 300 pmdiff2 scripts identical on Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain and 299 of 300 on Elysium, and 50 of 50 call semantics words. I reran pmdiff2 script 189 myself through tools/opdiff/pmdiff2.py with the same seed: Ethereum and Arbitrum One give the same output hash 545529ec198ae60b at 25 and 40 million gas, and Elysium gives empty output at 25 million and the same hash at 40 million. Binary search puts the gas needed at about 22.94 million on Arbitrum One and 26.29 million on Elysium. Elysium's cap is not 25 million: a GAS probe at a requested 60 million returned 49,979,000 remaining, so the 25 million limit is pmdiff2.py:172, not the endpoint. I found the cause of the extra gas. eth_getBalance and eth_getTransactionCount show precompiles 0x01 and 0x04 with zero balance and zero nonce on Elysium, and balances on Arbitrum One. A 1 wei CALL to 0x04 costs 6,839 gas on Arbitrum One and 31,839 on Elysium, and to 0x01 9,824 against 34,824, which is the 25,000 new account charge for an empty account. Script 189 is a native payout script (it sends value to 4 and 1), and a later call that uses all forwarded gas multiplies that difference by about 64 through the 63/64 rule. SSTORE, SLOAD, TSTORE, KECCAK256, cold CALL and LOG0 cost the same on both chains. The difference is account state, not an opcode rule. A transaction that runs short of gas reverts as a whole, and src/ keeps no partial state from a failed call (src/types/Currency.sol:48, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134 forward gas() and revert on failure), so the outputs computed are the same.
